title: Fixed time step game loop for canvas games
when: The user builds a canvas game and needs simulation speed that does not depend on the monitor refresh rate, with smooth drawing between simulation ticks.
inputs: simulation rate in ticks per second
prompt:
Goal: Game rules advance in equal ticks while drawing happens once per display frame, blended between ticks.
Steps:
1. In loop.js export start({ update, render, hz = 60 }) with const STEP = 1000 / hz in milliseconds.
2. In the requestAnimationFrame callback read the timestamp argument; frameMs = Math.min(timestamp - last, 250) so a long stall cannot spiral.
3. acc += frameMs; while (acc >= STEP) { copy positions to prev; update(STEP / 1000); acc -= STEP } with a cap of 5 ticks per frame, dropping the leftover.
4. alpha = acc / STEP; render(alpha) draws x = prev.x + (cur.x - prev.x) * alpha for moving objects.
5. update never draws and render never changes rules; random numbers are drawn only inside update.
6. Return stop(), which calls cancelAnimationFrame(handle); on resume set last = null so the first frame counts as 0 ms.
Quality bar:
- The same inputs give the same tick count and positions on 60, 120 and 144 Hz screens.
- No visible stutter at hz 30 thanks to interpolation.
- Tick work stays under 4 ms on a mid range phone.
Pitfalls:
- Date.now instead of the frame timestamp, which drifts and jitters.
- Multiplying by the raw frame delta, so collisions miss at low frame rates.
- No tick cap, so a slow device freezes inside a catch up loop.
Verify:
- [ ] With 4x CPU throttling the game speed stays equal.
- [ ] Pause then resume does not teleport objects.
- [ ] getContext("2d") and requestAnimationFrame are present.
Output: js/loop.js (start, stop), js/game.js (update, render) and index.html with the canvas.

examples.input: meu jogo fica mais rápido no monitor de 144 Hz
examples.output: loop.js with 60 Hz accumulator, tick cap, interpolated render, stop and resume
